name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite, and the binding constraint is financing, not saturation. Datacenter and robot ceilings are lifted an order of magnitude (60,000 TWh / 3,000 per 1000 workers) so they never bind within the horizon, and compute gains a cognitive labor payoff (aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh 1e5: today's ~500 TWh augments ~1% of the workforce; the baseline default is 0). Since the 2026 accounting reconciliation, automation energy is intermediate consumption in ALL scenarios and robots carry the Acemoglu-Restrepo payoff (2 worker-equivalents) by default, so this scenario's distinct levers are the lifted ceilings, the AI payoff, and the endogenous energy-capex share (cleanShareFlex 1, up to 60% of investment). Whether AI compute growth nets positive GDP depends on the payoff magnitude vs its energy cost — that tension is the point of the scenario. Uncalibrated hypothesis, not a forecast.
